structure: Part 12, Transporters (trade-imports-animals-frontend at main 4c2119da, tag 0.286.0). Read in full, under src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/: page.js (the five transporter page ids and slugs, plus the two part-11 pages), evaluation.js (the transport feature's obligation bindings), transporter-details-save.js (the save sequence shared by both add forms), copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js (only the transporters, transporterAdd, transportersSelect, commercialTransporterDetails and privateTransporterDetails keys are claimed here; portOfEntry and transitCountries belong to part 11), transporters/ (controller, template, rows.js, transporter-record.js, validate.js), transporter-add/, transporters-select/, commercial-transporter-details/ and private-transporter-details/ (controller and template each), and fit/transporters.fit.spec.js (9 describe blocks, 52 tests once the parametrised loops are expanded), fit/commercial-transporter-details.fit.spec.js (4 describe blocks, 27 tests expanded) and fit/axe.js. To state what the pages show, it also read the transporter service the pages call (src/server/app/services/transporters/index.js, records.js, register.js), the oneOf and maxText validators (src/server/app/lib/validate/validators.js), the shared oneOf default message (src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js), shared/save-actions.njk, and the transport entries in flow/flow.js, flow/task-rows.js and flow/section-captions (index.js and copy.en.js). Pages covered: /transporters (the transporter list: guidance, search, the six-column table with status tags, Add a transporter, save), /transporters/add (the transporter type chooser), /transporters/select (the approved commercial register, which nothing links to), /transporters/add/commercial (the add-commercial form with its Northern Ireland fixed country) and /transporters/add/private (the add-private form with its country select). Claims run in that page order: route and reach, heading and caption, copy, fields with labels, hints, options and whether required, validation messages verbatim, branches and where they lead, buttons and links, what is saved; then the organisation transporter store, the Welsh copy, and the fit tests (each test is cited in the ref of the claim it proves, and the accessibility and validation-pattern tests have claims of their own).
